reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I'll check the orders and refunds myself, since a recorded payout can't be undone.
The handoff says three refunds were applied, but I'll check the refund list directly before paying anyone, since payouts can't be recalled.
The refund list matches the handoff exactly, and each refund is smaller than its order, so nothing looks wrong. I'll get the net balance for each customer from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 24929 matches my own check: orders 220 and 223 total 58024, minus refunds 9480 and 23615 (33095), gives 24929. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 30973 matches my check: orders 221 and 224 total 30973 with no refunds against them. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.

Cobalt's net balance of 33028 matches my check: orders 222 and 225 total 63688, minus refund 30660 on order 222, gives 33028. All three balances now match my own arithmetic, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 24929 is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout of 30973, which matched my own check against the orders and refunds.
Birch's payout is recorded. Cobalt's net balance of 33028 matched my own check, so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched my own arithmetic against the orders and refunds, so the batch is complete.
